title: Reverse String II
summary: Given a string s and an integer k, reverse the first k characters for every 2k characters starting from the beginning of the string.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k, reverse the first k characters for every 2k characters starting from the beginning of the string. If fewer than k characters remain, reverse all of them. If between k and 2k characters remain, reverse the first k characters and leave the rest unchanged.
constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 10,000; lowercase English letters only; 1 <= k <= 10,000.
Partition positions into blocks of 2*k starting at index zero. Reverse the first k characters of each block and keep its second k unchanged.
If the last block has fewer than k characters, reverse all of them. Otherwise reverse just its first k. Return a new string.
hints: The decision to reverse alternates by k-sized regions, starting with a reversed region.
Visit starts 0,2k,4k,... and swap inward across at most k available characters.
For each start in steps of 2k, use left=start and right=min(start+k,n)-1; swap until left>=right.
The final short region needs no special extra loop: the clipped right endpoint handles it. Do not reverse the second half of any 2k block.
editorial: Each character lies in exactly one 2k block. Swapping its first min(k,remaining) characters realizes the required reversal while leaving the rest untouched. The mutable character buffer and returned string take O(n) space; all swaps together take O(n) time. The oracle independently computes the source index for each output position rather than swapping or slicing blocks.

tests.explanation: Blocks are abcd and efg. Reverse ab to ba and ef to fe, keeping cd and g unchanged: bacdfeg.
The first block abcdef becomes cbadef. Only gh remains, fewer than k characters, so reverse both: cbadefhg.
